title: A bounded ontology kernel survives two semantically different real domains
claim: Manufacturing and Project Ontology can both be expressed using the same frozen meta-model/resource kinds without adding kernel primitive kinds, domain-name compiler special cases, or domain-specific semantic operators.
null_hypothesis: The apparent kernel is only manufacturing-shaped; adding a research-project domain requires new primitive kinds or special-case semantics.
rivals: A conventional typed schema framework is equally bounded and the ontology kernel offers no special compositional advantage.
The kernel remains bounded only by moving domain semantics into opaque code that cannot be inspected as ontology resources.
mechanism: A genuinely general operational ontology should separate a small set of resource kinds/capabilities from unbounded domain vocabulary, allowing new domains to add declarations rather than new meta-level machinery.
scope: Frozen IR kernel and the complete Manufacturing + Project Ontology domain contracts.
predictions: Project Ontology adds only ordinary domain declarations: types, links, interfaces, functions, actions, policies, authorities, observations, constraints and adapters.
Kernel resource-kind count is unchanged after Domain 2.
Compiler/runtime core contains no condition keyed to manufacturing or project domain identity.
Cross-domain links can be declared without a new kernel primitive.
falsifiers: A Project Ontology requirement cannot be represented without adding a new kernel resource kind.
A compiler semantic branch keyed to the domain is required.
A concept claimed to be domain configuration actually changes generic runtime semantics.

experiment.summary: Freeze the kernel after Manufacturing, add the strong Project Ontology domain blind to kernel changes, and audit the semantic/runtime diff.
steps: Snapshot/freeze kernel schema and compiler dispatch table.
Implement Project Ontology only through allowed extension points.
Run static diff/audit for new kernel kinds and domain-keyed branches.
Generate mixed-domain legal definitions and compile/validate them.
Inject a fake domain-specific branch and prove the audit catches it.

oracle: Frozen list of kernel resource kinds plus static/dynamic dispatch audit and schema validation.
baseline: A conventional typed schema/plugin architecture subjected to the same Domain 2 requirements, used to contextualize whether boundedness is ontology-specific.

support_if: 0 new kernel primitive kinds after Project Ontology.
100% of registered Domain 2 requirements compile through allowed generic resource kinds.
reject_if: Any necessary new kernel primitive kind or domain-identity semantic branch is introduced.
inconclusive_if: Project Ontology implementation omits any required strong-model object/action/governance requirement.
invalid_if: Kernel freeze snapshot is changed after Domain 2 adaptation begins without a new experiment version.

python_hypothesis_role.strategy: Generate legal resource combinations from both domains and mixed cross-domain references to search generic compiler/validation assumptions.
python_hypothesis_role.mutation_proof: Inject a domain-name special case and a synthetic new primitive kind; static/property checks must fail.

stop_conditions: If a new primitive is genuinely required, reject/narrow bounded-kernel claim before adding it; record the proposed primitive for a new hypothesis version.
